review_correction: The initial two passing runs sampled cpu.stat before the fetch, so throttling could have occurred before the HTTP body was held. PR review identified that false-positive risk. The probe now samples after the first byte and starts the CPU helper only then; the two corrected runs below supersede the earlier measurements.
cleanup: No matching namespace or /etc/netns directory remained after the run; the transient user unit was stopped and reset.
local_checks: 46 Rust tests, 17 Python tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, bins/examples build, Python compile, JSON parse and diff check passed. The separate controlled netns suite passed 2233 MCP decisions on the same binary; its local log SHA-256 is ec74c1318c81087c030c1828e14fc775e2182c590db037cbb5a89736a241fca8.
scope: Real MCP modern stdio call, controlled DNS and HTTP inside a disposable route-free network namespace; fixture and server shared one 50% CPU user cgroup. The HTTP body was incomplete while kernel throttling was observed.
limitations: Finite local test using sudo for namespace setup/entry and a three-second CPU helper. No native-client delivery, cancellation under pressure, OOM/PID exhaustion, sustained load, generalized latency guarantee or release approval. CI does not run the user-systemd/namespace fixture.
